sources.short_quote: Token budget for storing individual tool/function outputs in history.
sources.paraphrase: The public reference describes a per-output history token budget, not a guaranteed UTF-8 output byte bound or this session’s effective budget. Installed 0.162.1 is separately fingerprinted; current website has no matching release stamp.
Current official JSON schema declares tool_output_token_limit an unsigned integer with minimum zero, no numeric default. This is not the installed tool definition.

Public Read documentation separates 25,000-token output and 256-KB whole-file input checks; it describes prefix paging on whole-file token overflow and errors on oversized explicit ranges. It dates allow_large to 2.1.296+, beyond installed 2.1.289. Bash/PowerShell successful output normally uses a roughly 30,000-character inline/readback window and a saved-file preview on overflow; failing output uses a roughly 10,000-character excerpt. bashOutputMaxChars changes the successful window, while BASH_MAX_OUTPUT_LENGTH alone changes readback. None of those character limits is a UTF-8 byte contract, or an observed call in this task.

The environment variable changes the Read token default. New allow_large behavior documented there is not re-certified for installed 2.1.289. Selected local environment/settings values are absent; this does not exclude another session’s per-call overrides.
